SF Gate

from the editor-in-chief

Wednesday, September 16, 2015

We're starting a news experiment at The San Francisco Chronicle, and we need you, our readers, to help make it a success.

Today we became the first newspaper-based media company to pursue crowdfunding with Beacon, an Oakland-based journalism startup. Our first collaboration will produce a multimedia project on issues surrounding immigration and the region's tech industry.

Specifically, we want to explore H-1B visas, the would-be immigrants who seek them and the companies that stand to benefit from a loosening of regulations. The political fervor around the issue has been fierce, but there has been little reporting about the lives affected both here and abroad.

The Chronicle is dedicated to Northern California and the Bay Area — to telling the complete truth about what is happening here. Sometimes to do that, we must look outside our borders.

From here in the Bay Area, we can tell part of the story of how the region's tech boom has come into conflict with U.S. immigration policy. We have done this again and again. This innovative crowdfunding approach will allow us to employ freelance journalists with expertise in international reporting while keeping our own reporters dedicated to uncovering wrongdoing in San Francisco and beyond and telling the stories that surface here, near our homes.

Beacon Reader will help us solicit up to $15,000 for this multimedia reporting effort. Chronicle editors and designers will prepare the stories for publication so that the money raised will pay for newsgathering.

Major funders will be unveiled after the reporting and editing is completed to ensure journalistic integrity. Significant donors will be acknowledged upon publication. We will share the story in print and online, reaching millions of readers around the world.

More than a century ago, the first editor of this company proclaimed that the San Francisco region deserved media that was "alarmingly enterprising, startlingly original, honest and fearless." That's never been more true, and we hope you agree this is an enterprising way to tell an original and fearlessly honest story about something that matters deeply to our community.

Become a backer and help us tell the broader story of the people impacted by the H-1B debate.

Audrey Cooper Editor-in-Chief San Francisco Chronical
